messages:
zoe: Quick sync  dashboard flagged a big RSVP spike for last week's launch webinar but downstream lead quality is softer than our benchmark narrative. Can @jamal pull source-level attribution and also a little cohort retention across 7 days? Need a concise blurb for the KPI review.

jamal: On it. Early read: organic RSVP -> demo request 6.5%, paid RSVP -> demo request 10.8%, but qualified lead (sales-ready) share is 2.1% overall. Paid volume higher but intent lower versus our last webinar benchmark. Ill push numbers to the dash.

ben: Two quick hypotheses: 1) messaging drift during the event (CTA moved from "Book demo" to "Try now"); 2) routing TTL sent many registrants into nurture and they never hit SDRs. Both would inflate RSVPs but depress QL.

priya: Noted on messaging. I checked the creative rotation: retargeting ads used variant C (broad copy) for 48h. I'll swap to variant D (qualification-first) and compress retarget window to 24h.

zoe: Also we needed a short launch-post benchmark note for comms: can someone pull prior three webinar benchmarks (RSVP->QL, CPL, 7d engagement) so we can say how this launch compares?

jamal: SQL used: ```select source, count(*) as rsvps, sum(case when demo_requested then 1 else 0 end) as demos, sum(case when qualified then 1 else 0 end) as ql from webinar_signups where event_date between '2026-02-01' and '2026-03-22' group by source;``` Pushing export to the dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/s/launch/benchmarks/1758887776 (CSV attached).

ben: One more data quirk to check: CRM mapping shows UTM_medium sometimes empty for organic partners. That breaks source parity. Jamal can you flag any rows where utm_medium is null but referral_host in ("partner.edu","community.io")?

jamal: Will include that in the export and add a small note to the KPI slides.

zoe: Ops plan: Jamal  assemble a 2-slide snapshot for KPI review: 1) benchmark table vs last 3 webinars, 2) routing & messaging impact with quick recs. Priya  swap retarget creative and post variants to #marketing. Ben  validate routing TTL change won't overload SDR queues. Maria  will lead the narrative for the review.

maria: Sounds good. For the narrative: we'll lead with the benchmark delta (higher RSVPs, lower QL), hypothesis -> data (source + routing + creative), and then a short ask: tighten prospecting + compress retarget + immediate routing for 24h with failover.

ben: I ran a quick capacity check: SDR max queue cushion is 60. If we immediate-route, add a fallback to `nurture-backfill` after 2h if queue > 45. I'll patch the playbook.

priya: Ad copy variants I'm posting: headline A: "Cut inference costs 40%"; headline B: "Ship production-ready features faster"; retarget copy will emphasize use-case and next-step (demo booking). Posting by 2pm ET.

dashbot: Snapshot + export: https://dash.redwood.ai/s/launch/benchmarks/1758887776  includes cohort retention (7d), source split, and quick CSV.

jamal: Added cohort `webinar: >2 actions` retention metric and a note: UTM parity issue with partner referrals. Will include a recommended mapping fix.

zoe: KPI review at 10:30am tomorrow. If anyone sees a >15% shift in QL before then, escalate in this thread and ping the oncall list. Also, Maria please include the launch-post benchmark paragraph for the comms draft so we can share after the sync.

maria: Will do. Draft for the comms paragraph: "Compared to our trailing three webinars, this launch delivered 38% more RSVPs but a 22% lower qualified-lead rate. Early signals point to broader prospecting and in-event CTA wording as primary drivers; recommended mitigations: tighten lookalike thresholds, compress retarget, and immediate routing for 24h. We'll monitor the SDR funnel and report back at the KPI review."

ben: Patch to routing applied (temp). I added failover rule to route to `nurture-backfill` after 2h or if queue>45. Posting log: ```PATCH /playbooks/route/webinar_reg {"routing":"immediate","failover":"nurture-backfill","threshold":45}```

priya: Creative posted to #marketing. Also added a small A/B with different CTAs for retargeting: demo-first vs ROI-first.

zoe: Great work team. See you all at review. :rocket:
